newsitem.title: USA: Former Cub Scout Clinton lauds service by scouts.
newsitem.headline: Former Cub Scout Clinton lauds service by scouts.

text.p: - Former Cub Scout Bill Clinton Wednesday told an audience of 29,000 Boy Scouts that their service to America should serve as an example to others.
"Character counts and service counts," President Clinton told the quadrennial national Scout Jamboree.
Clinton's speech to the group echoed themes sounded at the April presidential summit on volunteerism in Philadelphia, at which Americans were urged to volunteer their time in service of others.
"I hope you will go home and help others to serve and learn the joy that you share by the service you do," Clinton said.
Clinton told the group he had been a Cub Scout while a boy in Arkansas.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters earlier that Clinton did not continue in the organisation and become a Boy Scout.
"I think he gave up the Boy Scouts for politics, probably," McCurry told reporters.
